card.statement:
(1)

Similarly we have a “Whittaker vector for the current $\eta(z)$ ”. Since $H[B_{\lambda};u]=1/\prod_{s\in\lambda}(1-uq^{j(s)-1}t^{1-i(s)})$, it is natural to set

$\begin{split}v^{(\infty)}_{m}:=&\sum_{\lambda\,\vdash m}J_{\lambda}(q,t)\dfrac{q^{n(\lambda^{\prime})}}{\langle J_{\lambda}(q,t),J_{\lambda}(q,t)\rangle_{q,t}}\dfrac{1}{\prod_{s\in\lambda}q^{j(s)-1}t^{1-i(s)}}\\
=&\sum_{\lambda\,\vdash m}J_{\lambda}(q,t)\dfrac{t^{n(\lambda)}}{\langle J_{\lambda}(q,t),J_{\lambda}(q,t)\rangle_{q,t}}.\end{split}$

(3.19)

Then for each $n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$ we have

$\displaystyle\eta_{d}v_{n+1}^{(\infty)}=\begin{cases}v_{n}^{(\infty)}&(d=1)\\
0&(d\geq 2).\end{cases}$

(3.20)

The proof of this formula is similar to that for $v^{(0)}_{n}$, so we only give an outline. Set

$v^{(\infty)}(w):=\sum_{n\geq 0}v_{n}^{(\infty)}w^{n}$

Using the specialization $\varepsilon_{0,t}$ of the Cauchy kernel, we can prove

$v^{(\infty)}(w)=\exp\Bigl(\sum_{n>0}\dfrac{1}{1-q^{n}}\dfrac{p_{n}}{n}w^{n}\Bigr).$

Then the relation (3.20) follows from the following relation of operators acting on $\cal{F}$.

$\eta(z)v^{(\infty)}(w)=(1-w/z)v^{(\infty)}(w)\eta(z).$

(2)

Using the operator $\nabla$ (3.8), we have

$\displaystyle v_{n}^{(\infty)}=\nabla^{-1}v_{n}^{(0)}.$

(3.21)

Then the relation (3.20) can be shown by (3.9) and the Whittaker relation (3.16) for $v_{n}^{(0)}$.

3.3. Part 3 of the proof

3.3.1. Preparations

Before dealing with the remaining relations

$\displaystyle\bigl((q/t)^{d-1}\eta_{d}\Delta_{h_{r-1}}+D_{d}\Delta_{h_{r}}\bigr)v_{n}^{(0)}=0\quad(d\geq 2,\ r\geq 0)$

in Corollary 2.6, we prepare some lemmas. Let us recall several notations.

$\displaystyle D(z)=\sum_{d\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}}D_{d}z^{-d}=\exp\Bigl(\sum_{n>0}(1-q^{n})\partial_{p_{n}}z^{-n}\Bigr),$

$\displaystyle\eta(z)=\exp\Bigl(\sum_{n>0}(1-t^{-n})\dfrac{p_{n}}{n}z^{n}\Bigr)\exp\Bigl(-\sum_{n>0}(1-q^{n})\partial_{p_{n}}z^{-n}\Bigr),$

$\displaystyle v^{(0)}(w)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}(-w)^{n}v^{(0)}_{n}=\exp\Bigl(-\sum_{n>0}\dfrac{1}{1-q^{n}}\dfrac{p_{n}}{n}w^{-n}\Bigr).$
card.label: Remark 3.7

paper.title: Whittaker vector of deformed Virasoro algebra and Macdonald symmetric functions
paper.abstract: We give a proof of Awata and Yamada's conjecture for the explicit formula of Whittaker vector of the deformed Virasoro algebra realized in the Fock space. The formula is expressed as a summation over Macdonald symmetric functions with factored coefficients. In the proof we fully use currents appearing in the Fock representation of Ding-Iohara-Miki quantum algebra. We also mention an interpretation of Whittaker vector in terms of the geometry of the Hilbert schemes of points on the affine plane.
